one_sentence_story: At Stanford in 2023, two tiny 64-pin sensors on the speech movement strip of a 68-year-old woman paralyzed by ALS translated her silent attempts to speak into text at 62 words per minute.
so_what_for_you: Even when disease cuts the wire from brain to vocal cords for over a decade, the brain's speech movement strip keeps forming every syllable clearly — and modern neural interfaces can give that voice back.
